memory_verse: "He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit." —Romans 8:11, NASB
sermon_title: A Freedom Only Christ Can Give

days.focus: The Law's Limit: What It Cannot Free You From
days.reflection_question: Romans 8:4 says the righteous requirement of the law is fulfilled in us who walk by the Spirit, and Romans 8:11 says the same Spirit who raised Christ actually lives in you now — so when you honestly review yesterday and today, are you drawing on that resurrection-level power in the moments you feel enslaved to a specific attitude or habit, or are you still trying to manage it through willpower and external behavior, the way the law of Moses would?

days.focus: The Inside of the Cup: What God Actually Sees
days.reflection_question: Ezekiel 36:27 promises that God's Spirit will cause you to walk in His statutes from the inside out, which is exactly what Romans 8:11 points to — the Spirit giving life to what is mortal and dead within you — so where specifically in your inner life this week, in thoughts, motives, or attitudes no one else has seen, are you allowing the Spirit to do that deep work rather than settling for an outward tidiness that God does not accept?

days.focus: Jesus Came to Proclaim Release to the Captives
days.reflection_question: Second Corinthians 3:17 says where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom, and Romans 8:11 roots that freedom in the very Spirit who raised a dead body to life — so are you treating the Holy Spirit's presence in you as a real and sufficient power to actually liberate you from a specific bondage you keep returning to, or have you mentally reduced Him to a comforting presence while you continue managing sin on your own terms?

days.focus: Do You Wish to Be Well? Honest Desire Before God
days.reflection_question: Galatians 5:16 gives a direct promise: walk by the Spirit and you will not carry out the desire of the flesh — and Romans 8:11 tells you the Spirit capable of raising the dead is the very one indwelling you — so is there a specific sin or craving you have quietly made peace with after years of trying, and if Jesus stood before you today and asked 'Do you wish to be well?' would your honest answer be yes, or have you settled for managing the outside while leaving that thing untouched inside?

days.focus: God's Opinion Versus the Opinion of Others
days.reflection_question: Jesus says in John 6:63 that it is the Spirit who gives life and the flesh counts for nothing, which directly echoes Romans 8:11's contrast between mortal flesh and the life the Spirit imparts — so when you made choices this week about how to speak, respond, or act, were you genuinely seeking what God who sees in secret thinks of your inner motivation, or were you primarily managing how you appear to people around you, and can you name one specific moment where those two pulled in different directions?

days.focus: Real Freedom Through His Spirit: From Memory Verse to Lived Reality
days.reflection_question: First Peter 3:18 says Christ was put to death in the flesh but made alive in the Spirit, the same resurrection dynamic Romans 8:11 says is now at work in your mortal body — as you review the whole week, can you identify one area of your inner life, a thought pattern, an attitude, an unforgiving feeling, a secret craving, where you genuinely allowed the Spirit to give life this week rather than just keeping the outside of the cup presentable, and what would it look like to yield that same area to Him fully starting tomorrow?
